gloss: to trample; to tread down; to devastate

definitions.gloss: to trample; to tread down; to walk all over and damage
definitions.explanation: To step on and damage something, especially plants, fields, or ground, by walking or stepping on them roughly. Can also be used figuratively for devastating or laying waste to an area.

examples.japanese: {花壇|かだん}を{踏|ふ}み{荒|あ}らされた。
{子供|こども}たちが{芝生|しばふ}を{踏|ふ}み{荒|あ}らしてしまった。
{鹿|しか}の{群|む}れが{畑|はたけ}に{入|はい}り{込|こ}んで、{作物|さくもつ}を{踏|ふ}み{荒|あ}らしていった。
examples.english: A herd of deer broke into the field and trampled the crops.

notes:
Compound verb of {踏|ふ}む (to step on) and {荒|あ}らす (to lay waste, to damage). A godan verb conjugating with the {荒|あ}らす ending.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive. Takes を to mark the thing being trampled.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {花壇|かだん}を{踏|ふ}み{荒|あ}らす: to trample a flower bed
- {畑|はたけ}を{踏|ふ}み{荒|あ}らす: to trample a field
- {芝生|しばふ}を{踏|ふ}み{荒|あ}らす: to trample a lawn
- {庭|にわ}を{踏|ふ}み{荒|あ}らす: to trample a garden

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {踏|ふ}みつける: to stamp on, to trample — focuses on stepping on with force
- {荒|あ}らす: to lay waste, to devastate — broader term for destruction
- {踏|ふ}みにじる: to trample, to violate — often used figuratively for trampling on rights or dignity
